title: MC-E2E (+ MC-SEEDS): does the multi-corpus router survive when the cell must be INFERRED rather than given? (+ three-seed replication; zero calls)
question: The same policies as MC-ROUTER applied through the taxonomy's own flatLeaf prediction over the 143 federated leaves (predicted source / source+domain / leaf) at seeds 42 / 137 / 2048, query-level bootstrap 200 resamples per seed: (1) the deployed router beats the best single model by > 2 SE in all three seeds; (2) the metadata cost (oracle-cell gain minus predicted-cell gain) per seed; (3) the across-seed spread < the within-seed SE.

plain_description.what: Runs the multi-corpus router end to end. The question's cell is predicted by the tree instead of given, then the policy picks a model. It is compared with the best single model over three random seeds. No calls.
plain_description.why: It checks whether the routing gain survives when the cell must be inferred in practice.
plain_description.information: A gain above noise at every seed would make routing usable. Result: the router beats the best single model in all three seeds (about +3.4 points as first read). But the gain varies between seeds more than the noise level, so its size is not seed-stable. Corrections: the analysis drew its own split, so about 70% of the questions it scored had been training data for the taxonomy. A later clean re-read on the split of record gives +2.9 points [+1.8, +4.0], and the cost of inferring the cell is neither shown nor ruled out. The routing tree also had about 6.7% of the routed questions visible during construction. An early figure (+4.1) was superseded. The pool is checked by question id only, not by content.
